title: メールの型（6パーツ）
note: あいさつ → 書き出し → 目的 → 事情説明 → お願い → 締め。7分・100〜150語が目安。
text:
Dear Professor Brown,
I hope this message finds you well, and I am sorry to take up your time.
I am writing to ask about the assignment that is due next week.
The reason I am asking is that I was sick for several days and missed two classes.
Would it be possible for you to give me a few extra days to finish it?
Thank you very much for your time and understanding.
Best regards,
Ken

title: メールの便利表現
note: 目的・説明・依頼・締めで使い回せるフレーズ。
text:
I am writing to let you know that the heater in my room is not working.
I wanted to follow up on the email I sent last Monday.
To give you some background, I recently joined the photography club.
As a result, I have not been able to sleep well this week.
In addition, the window in the kitchen does not close properly.
Would you mind sending me the updated schedule?
I would really appreciate it if you could reply by Friday.
Please let me know if you need any further information.
I look forward to hearing from you soon.

title: 模範メール：騒音の相談（オリジナル）
note: 課題例：寮の隣室がうるさい。状況説明・影響・解決策の提案。
text:
Dear Ms. Carter,
I hope you are doing well, and I apologize for bothering you. I live in Room 304 of West Hall, and I am writing to ask for your help with a noise problem. For the past two weeks, the students in the room next to mine have been playing loud music until two or three in the morning. As a result, I have been very tired during my morning classes, and my grades have started to suffer. I have already spoken with them politely, but nothing has changed. Would it be possible for you to remind them about the quiet hours? Alternatively, if there is an empty room on another floor, I would be happy to move. Thank you very much for taking the time to read this.
Sincerely,
Ken Sato

title: 模範メール：イベント参加の依頼（オリジナル）
note: 課題例：地元の専門家に学内イベントで話してもらう依頼。
text:
Dear Dr. Rivera,
I hope this email finds you well. My name is Ken Sato, and I am a member of the Environmental Club at Lakeside University. I am writing to invite you to speak at our Earth Day event on April 22. Our club has been reading about your research on urban gardens, and many students are eager to learn how they can start similar projects on campus. Your talk would only need to be about thirty minutes, followed by a short question-and-answer session. We would, of course, be glad to cover your travel costs. Would you be available on that date? If so, please reply to this email or call me at the number below.
Thank you for considering our invitation.
Best regards,
Ken Sato

title: ディスカッションの型（5ステップ）
note: 意見 → 理由 → 具体例 → 他の学生への言及 → 補足。10分・100語以上が目安。
text:
From my perspective, (my opinion on the topic).
The main reason I feel this way is that (specific reason).
To give an example, (a concrete example or personal experience).
I understand why (student's name) believes (their idea), but I think this view overlooks an important point.
In other words, (expand on your reason with one more detail).

title: 模範投稿：宿題は必要か（オリジナル）
note: 教授の問い：小学校で毎日の宿題をやめるべきか。
text: From my perspective, elementary schools should not stop giving homework completely. The main reason I feel this way is that short daily assignments help children build good study habits early in life. To give an example, when I was in elementary school, I had to read for twenty minutes every evening, and that simple routine made me enjoy books for the rest of my life. I understand why Emma believes that homework causes stress for young children, but I think this view overlooks an important point. In other words, the problem is not homework itself but the amount of it. If teachers keep assignments short and meaningful, students can gain the benefits without feeling overwhelmed.

title: 模範投稿：オンライン授業（オリジナル）
note: 教授の問い：大学の講義は今後オンラインが中心になるべきか。
text: In my opinion, universities should combine online and in-person classes rather than move everything online. My main reason is that face-to-face discussion is difficult to replace. For instance, in my sociology seminar last year, the most valuable moments came from unplanned conversations with classmates after the lecture ended. These conversations helped me understand ideas that I had not fully grasped from the readings. Jason makes a fair point that online lectures save time and money, especially for students who live far from campus. However, I believe that a purely online system would make students feel isolated. A balanced approach, where lectures are recorded but seminars stay on campus, would give students the best of both worlds.

title: Q1（個人の経験）の型
note: ①答える → ②具体例 → ③その理由。45秒、準備時間なし。
text:
Yes, I have, and one experience that comes to mind is (your answer).
For example, (a specific situation with details).
I think I remember this so clearly because (the reason it mattered to you).

title: Q2（好み）の型
note: ①好みを言う → ②理由 → ③個人的な例 → ④例と立場を結ぶ。
text:
Personally, I would rather (your preference),
mainly because (your reason).
For instance, (a short personal story).
That experience taught me that (connect the story to your preference).

title: Q3（未来の予想）の型
note: ①意見 → ②理由 → ③最近の傾向 → ④意見と結ぶ。
text:
Yes, I do think (your prediction will happen). / No, I don't think (it will happen).
One reason is that (your reason).
These days, (a current trend you have noticed).
Given this trend, it seems likely that (connect the trend to your prediction).

title: Q4（抽象的な考え）の型
note: ①賛否 → ②理由 → ③例 → ④まとめ。
text:
I strongly agree that (the idea). / I don't really believe that (the idea).
The reason is that (your reason).
To illustrate, (an example from your life or society).
So overall, I am convinced that (restate your opinion).

title: 模範解答：Q1 運動習慣（オリジナル）
note: Q：普段どんな運動をしますか？
text: Yes, I try to exercise a few times a week, and the activity I enjoy most is swimming. For example, every Tuesday and Thursday morning, I go to the pool at my university before my first class. I usually swim for about forty minutes, and then I feel awake and ready to study. I think swimming became my favorite because I hurt my knee playing soccer in high school, and my doctor told me swimming was easier on my joints. So it started as a kind of medical advice, but now it's honestly one of the best parts of my week.

title: 模範解答：Q4 SNSと人間関係（オリジナル）
note: Q：SNSは人をつなぐか、孤立させるか。
text: I honestly think social media does both, but overall I believe it connects people more than it isolates them. The reason is that it lets us keep relationships that would otherwise disappear. To illustrate, when I moved to a new city for university, I was worried about losing touch with my high school friends. But because we have a group chat, we still share photos and talk almost every day, and when I go home, it feels like we were never apart. Of course, if someone spends all day scrolling instead of meeting people, that can be lonely. So overall, I'm convinced that social media is a useful tool, as long as people use it to support real relationships rather than replace them.

title: つなぎ言葉（機能別）
note: Speaking・Writing 共通。各行の機能を言えるようにする。
text:
Adding: in addition, furthermore, on top of that, what's more
Examples: for example, for instance, to illustrate, a good example is
Opinion: in my view, from my perspective, I would argue that, it seems to me that
Emphasis: in fact, above all, especially, what I mean is
Cause and effect: as a result, therefore, because of this, that's why
Contrast: however, on the other hand, even so, while, although
Sequence: first, after that, eventually, in the end
Conclusion: overall, all in all, in short, to sum up
